bear.argument: Costco is a risky investment because its results rest on a narrow base and a thin margin. The filing states that U.S. and Canadian operations comprised 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income in 2026, and that California alone was 26% of U.S. net sales, so a slowdown in one state or region would hit the whole company. The business is described as operating on very low margins, where modest changes in merchandise costs or SG&A can have substantial impacts on net income. Gross margin percentage fell three basis points to 11.09%, and the filing says the price of the stock already reflects high market expectations, with any miss potentially driving the stock lower. Growth also carries rising costs: capex is planned at about $7,500 in 2027, up from $6,435, and new warehouses face cannibalization and lower initial profitability. Finally, 2026 earnings were lifted by one-time IEEPA tariff refunds of $184, and the company says some of that money went back into member price reductions.

claims.claim: Heavy concentration in U.S. and Canadian operations and in California creates single-region exposure.
claims.quote: U.S. and Canadian operations, which comprised 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income in 2026

claims.claim: The business runs on very low margins, so small cost changes can move net income a lot.
claims.quote: Because our business operates on very low margins, modest changes in various items in the consolidated statements of income, particularly merchandise costs and SG&A expenses, can have substantial impacts on net income.

claims.claim: The stock price already reflects high expectations, raising the downside if results disappoint.
claims.quote: We believe that the price of our stock currently reflects high market expectations for our future operating results.

bull.argument: Costco's 2026 results show a business compounding on multiple fronts. Net sales rose 10% to $297,247 and net income rose 14% to $9,226, or $20.76 per diluted share. Comparable sales grew 8%, with average ticket up 5% and shopping frequency up 3%, meaning both existing and new members are spending more per visit and coming more often. Membership fee revenue grew 11% to $5,907, and the filing notes renewal rates of 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada. The balance sheet is strengthening: operating cash flow rose to $15,817 from $13,335, and cash and short-term investments reached $21,301. The Board also raised the quarterly dividend 13%. The opponent's concern about the very low margin is real, but management explicitly chose this model, and gross margin excluding gasoline inflation actually rose 10 basis points to 11.22%. Concentration risk is disclosed, not hidden, and the company is funding its growth internally.

claims.claim: Comparable sales growth was broad-based, driven by both ticket size and visit frequency.
claims.quote: Comparable sales were positively impacted by increases of 5% in average ticket and 3% in shopping frequency.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow grew strongly, funding investment and shareholder returns internally.
claims.quote: The increase was primarily due to higher operating income, as well as reduced net investment in merchandise inventories.

claims.claim: Underlying gross margin improved when gasoline inflation is excluded, countering the reported three basis point decline.
claims.quote: Excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation on net sales, gross margin percentage was 11.22%, an increase of 10 basis points.

bear.argument: The bull case rests on figures that the filing itself qualifies. Net sales rose 10%, but the MD&A says higher gasoline prices added $3,501, or 130 basis points, and currency added $1,332. Excluding gasoline, the 11.22% margin rose only 10 basis points, while reported gross margin fell three basis points to 11.09%. Net income growth of 14% also leans on $184 of one-time IEEPA tariff refunds, and the company says a portion was reinvested in member price cuts. Comparable sales growth excluding gasoline and currency was 7% in 2026, the same as 2025, and Canada's comparable sales ex-currency and gasoline fell from 8% to 7%. Membership renewal slipped to 89.8% worldwide, and the filing says the fee increase drove about 30% of membership income growth, versus 40% the prior year. Cash of $21,301 is real, but capex is planned to rise to about $7,500 and the company says there can be no assurance current expectations will be realized. Concentration is disclosed, but disclosure does not reduce exposure to California and Canada.

claims.claim: Reported gross margin fell, and the improvement cited depends on an adjusted figure.
claims.quote: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points; it increased 10 basis points excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation

claims.claim: Net income growth was helped by one-time tariff refunds, some of which went back to members as price cuts.
claims.quote: A portion of these refunds was invested in reducing prices for members.

claims.claim: Planned capital spending rises, and the company does not guarantee its expectations will be met.
claims.quote: There can be no assurance that current expectations will be realized, and plans are subject to change

bull.argument: The opponent is right that gasoline and currency flatter headline sales, and the filing says so. But the core trend is steadier than the critique suggests. Comparable sales excluding gasoline and currency held at 7% in both 2026 and 2025, so the underlying business did not decelerate. Canada's ex-items comparable sales eased from 8% to 7%, a modest dip rather than a break. The renewal decline is explained by the filing itself: worldwide renewal is hurt by international growth and online sign-ups, while U.S. and Canadian renewal stayed at 92.3%. The fee-driven share of membership growth falling from 40% to 30% still leaves a growing base of paying members. The $184 tariff refund is small relative to $9,226 of net income, and the company says most refunds go back to members. Cash of $21,301 was built from $15,817 of operating cash flow, which covers the planned $7,500 of capex. The risks are real, but the cash generation and stable underlying comparables support the investment case.

claims.claim: Underlying comparable sales growth, excluding gasoline and currency, was steady year over year.
claims.quote: Increases in comparable sales excluding the impact of changes in foreign-currency and gasoline prices (1) : U.S. 7 % 7 % 5 %

claims.claim: Lower worldwide renewal reflects international expansion and online mix rather than weakening U.S. and Canadian member loyalty.
claims.quote: Our worldwide renewal rate is adversely impacted by membership growth in certain international markets

claims.claim: Cash and investment balances grew, providing funding for the planned capital spending.
claims.quote: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments were $21,301 and $15,284 at August 30, 2026

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes from the filing, with the bull leaning on comparable-sales and cash flow strength and the bear on margin fragility, renewal slippage, and tariff-refund dependence. The bull's round-2 rebuttal effectively reframes the renewal decline and the fee share of growth, but it does not fully address the bear's point that reported gross margin fell and that the bear's ex-gasoline figures come from the company's own adjusted metrics. The bear's argument on concentration and one-time items is well-sourced, but its claim that cash balance is 'real' while planned capex rises is a weaker point, so the debate is close to even.
